newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southwest spot power down amid plant restarts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southwest spot power down amid plant restarts.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Southwest prices fell amid the restart of several generating plants while Northwest prices held steady, markets sources said Monday.

Traders said California-Oregon border (COB) prices dipped in early trade, but moved back up to Friday levels after the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) announced it had no surplus power for Tuesday schedulings.
BPA has not offered surplus power since late last week.
Next-day firm COB during peak demand hours was last quoted at $24.50-25.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), little changed from Friday. Off-peak COB was also steady at $17.50-18.00.
Firm on-peak power at Mid-Columbia was quoted $22.50-23.00 per MWh, also unchanged.
But spot power prices at the Palo Verde substation in Arizona "got crushed" Monday by a lack of buying interest from utilities, said one trade source.

Restart of the 1,080 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California as well as the 1,221 MW unit 1 at Palo Verde were cited as contributing to the lack of surplus power demand in the Southwest.
Furthermore, unit 1 at the San Juan coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was back on line Monday after being shut early Thursday.
This was said to have contributed to slightly lower next-day prices at Four Corners of around $22.00-25.00.
Firm, peak next-day Palo Verde was quoted $21.00-22.00, down from $23.00-24.00 on Friday.
Cash Palo Verde for the balance of November was quoted $20.60-21.00, down from $22.00-23.75 on Friday.
COB for November was quoted $22.25-22.75 per MWh, also down from Friday quotes.
